purpose: Four PLI Medical Devices scheme beneficiaries with confirmed Indian manufacturing subsidiaries and real disbursed/approved government incentive money (per docs/PLI_SCHEME_BENEFICIARY_LEADS.md Part 5C, source LS USQ 1001, 24.07.2026) do not appear in the current 263-company layer-16 lead list. This checks, per company, whether that is a genuine gap in the confirmed parent's own annual-report disclosure, or a gap in how the layer-16 sweep was built -- and separately whether the parent would even pass the layer-16 'verified-profitable' screen (margin>0 AND ROE>0, per scripts/build_leads.py line 6/85-86) in the first place.
method: For each of the 4 companies: (1) confirmed the exact listed/reporting parent via the company's own IR/corporate-structure disclosure, not assumption; (2) fetched that parent's most recent live annual report / 10-K / integrated report (SEC EDGAR for the US filer, direct corporate/investor-relations PDF for the three non-US filers -- akamai-gated omron.com PDFs required a reader-proxy fetch after direct curl/WebFetch were blocked, recorded below); (3) full-text-searched for every 'India' occurrence and classified each as context_only (country-list / disease-stats / bio, the Switzerland-sweep exclusion bar) vs genuine (named manufacturing/capacity/investment/strategic commentary); (4) computed net margin and ROE from the parent's own reported net income, revenue, and equity figures (or used the company's own reported ROE line where the AR states it directly) to independently apply the layer-16 screen; (5) where genuine evidence exists, extracted a real quoted sentence with exact source. No figures fabricated -- where extraction failed (Siemens/Omron PDFs first attempt) the raw PDF was downloaded and run through pdftotext locally, or refetched via a text-extraction proxy, rather than guessed.
layer16_screen_recap: scripts/build_leads.py: 'yfinance-verified profitable: profit_margin>0 AND roe>0' (line 6); score formula weights margin (capped 0.25) and roe (capped 0.30) at 20 points each. A parent that fails margin>0 AND roe>0 is excluded from layer 16 by design, regardless of how strong its India disclosure is.

recommendation.verdict: ADD, with a sourcing caveat noted for whoever edits layer 16
recommendation.reasoning: Omron Corporation (the actual TSE-listed, audited, profitability-screened parent) passes the screen and does have one genuine, non-context-only India mention in its own Integrated Report 2025. That single line is enough to clear the evidence bar the Switzerland sweep set (a real, specific facility commitment beats a country-list mention), which is why this is recommended for addition rather than logged as a null result. But the richer, more relevant evidence for a medical-devices lead -- the actual BP-monitor factory -- lives one level down at Omron Healthcare Co., Ltd.'s own press channel, not in the parent's investor-facing document. Whoever adds this to layers/16_leads.json should decide explicitly whether the evidence field cites the thin-but-parent-level Automation Center line or the richer-but-subsidiary-level factory quote; both are genuine, but they are not interchangeable in terms of which corporate voice is speaking.

summary.overall_finding: This was a genuine sweep gap, not a research gap or a uniform screen-driven exclusion. Three of the four parents (Siemens Healthineers, Nipro, Omron) both pass the layer-16 profitability screen and carry real, specific, non-context-only India manufacturing/investment/strategic disclosure in their own most recent annual reports -- they should have been in the 263-company list on the merits and were not, most likely because the layer-16 sweep's source corpus (yfinance-derived roster + 10-K/AR full-text sweep, per docs/LEADS.md's stated method) either did not cover these three tickers or did not surface their India mentions. Only Varex is correctly absent under the current methodology, and only because of a real FY2025 GAAP net loss (goodwill impairment) -- its own India-manufacturing disclosure is in fact the strongest and most concrete of the four (it is the only one of the four with an owned, not leased, Indian facility named directly in Item 2 Properties).
